title: What happens in read()?
question: A program reads 64 bytes of a file. Which parts of the kernel does that go through? (Here the file is in memory: no disk.)

stops.note: The syscall: the fd turns into the open file (a struct file), and the position to read at.
The VFS, the same for every file system: is the file open for reading, is the range sane? Then the file system's own read.
The page cache: a file's data lives in memory pages. Find the page at the position, and copy from it to the program. (In ramfs, the pages are all the file is.)
